pr_summary: Fix mx.random.normal producing -inf/inf values for half-precision dtypes (float16, bfloat16) by adding above_minus_one() helper in mlx/random.cpp to properly handle lower bound for these types
candidate_build_commands: mkdir -p build && cd build && cmake .. -DMLX_BUILD_METAL=OFF && make -j
candidate_activation_checks: python3 -c "import mlx.core as mx; a = mx.random.normal(dtype=mx.float16); print(a)"
patch_file_cues: mlx/random.cpp: adds above_minus_one() template helper for half-precision types
mlx/random.cpp: modifies normal() function to use dtype-specific lower bound
test_file_cues: tests/random_tests.cpp: test random normal with float16/bfloat16 checks abs(out) < inf
platform_constraint_evidence: CMakeLists.txt supports Linux/macOS with MLX_BUILD_METAL option for GPU
CircleCI config shows linux_build_and_test job with -DMLX_BUILD_METAL=OFF
README states MLX is 'prioritised for Apple silicon' but builds on Linux
Fix patch touches mlx/random.cpp which is platform-agnostic C++ code
Test file python/tests/test_random.py runs on Linux in CI
notes: MLX is Apple's machine learning framework optimized for Apple silicon but supports Linux builds without Metal GPU. The fix in mlx/random.cpp addresses half-precision random number generation by adding above_minus_one() helper. Tests exist in both Python (python/tests/test_random.py) and C++ (tests/random_tests.cpp). Linux builds require disabling Metal: CMAKE_ARGS="-DMLX_BUILD_METAL=OFF".
